name: Smash
summary: A fast, flat hit to finish a high ball.
whenToUse: When the ball comes high: a lob, a mistake, or a weak return that bounces above the net.

keyPoints.stance: Feet apart, right foot back (left foot if left-handed); move so the ball comes down in front of you.
keyPoints.bodyAction: Turn back with the ball, then a strong turn through it, weight to the front foot.
keyPoints.strokeLength: Long: from shoulder height to across the body.
keyPoints.timing: At the top of the bounce.
keyPoints.tablePosition: Wherever the ball is: move to it first.
keyPoints.freeArm: Up and pointing at the ball, then pulls in.
keyPoints.batArm: Bat high, flat or slightly closed; hit through the ball.
keyPoints.recovery: Ready for a lob coming back.
keyPoints.anticipation: A lob with heavy topspin kicks forward: give yourself room.

learningPath.task: Watch the turn and the flat hit.
learningPath.passCheck: You can say the three cues.
3 sets of 10, then yes to all self-checks.
selfChecks: Did you turn back before hitting?
Was the bat flat at contact?

learningPath.task: Drive the normal balls, smash the high ones.

gamePatterns.situation: Your opponent lobs from far back.
gamePatterns.how: Smash wide to the angles or into the body; don't smash at them twice in the same place.

causes: Hitting too early on the way up
fixes: Keep the bat flat or a bit closed
Wait for the top of the bounce
Move so you meet it higher

troubleshooting.symptom: I miss the high kicking balls

penholdNotes: Same action; penholders can also use the wrist to angle the smash.
